draft.title: Developing an argument across paragraphs
card: An essay argues one main idea, the thesis. Each body paragraph should add a new step to that argument, so the essay builds rather than repeats.
a paragraph that makes the same point as the one before, only with a new quote. The reader learns nothing new about the thesis.
a paragraph that takes the earlier point further. It might add a complication, a change over time or a deeper reason.
Ordering points from simpler to more complex helps. Start with the clearest idea, then move to ones that need more thought. Short link sentences show how each paragraph grows from the last.
draft.remember: Each paragraph should take the argument one step further, not say it again.

a.q: Which body paragraph best develops an argument, rather than repeating it?
opts: It builds on the last point by showing a complication
It restates the last point using a different quotation
It describes the plot in the order the events happen
It repeats the thesis word for word at the start
a.why: A developing paragraph adds a new step, such as a complication, to what came before. A new quotation for the same point is still repetition, which is the most tempting wrong option here.
a.clue: Look for the paragraph that adds something new to the argument.

b.q: Priya's essay argues that a novel's narrator becomes less trustworthy over time. Her paragraphs say: 1) the narrator is unreliable early, 2) the narrator is unreliable in the middle, 3) the narrator is unreliable late. What is the main weakness?
opts: Each paragraph repeats the point instead of building on it
The paragraphs are not in the order of the novel's events
The essay has too many paragraphs about the narrator
The thesis is about the narrator and not the plot
b.why: All three paragraphs make the same point, so the argument does not move forward. Following the order of the novel is not the problem: a change over time can suit that order, as long as each paragraph adds a new step.
b.clue: Ask what each paragraph adds that the last one did not.

a.best: It builds on the last point by showing a complication

b.best: Each paragraph repeats the point instead of building on it
